title: Extensible Terraform overlay strategy for customer-specific VPC parameters and upgrade-safe overrides
creator: Asha Menon
description: Design and implement an extensible pattern for customer-specific Terraform customizations for Private/VPC deployments. The goal is to support safe per-customer parameterization, local override files, and upgrade-safe module versioning while keeping the core module stable and auditable.
problem_statement: Customers require small, controlled deviations from the platform's baseline VPC wiring (subnet choices, routing, NAT behavior, security group attachments, peering configs). Current ad-hoc overlays lead to drift, upgrade friction, and expensive manual interventions during runtime upgrades and security patches.
proposed_solution: Introduce a three-layer composition: (1) core tenant module (stable public interface) maintained by Redwood, (2) customer overlay layer that provides lightweight variable patches and resource 'shim' modules, and (3) per-deployment local patch file for emergency fixes. Implement a merging strategy with clear precedence and tooling (overlay-gen) to render final tfvars and generate a signed plan artifact prior to apply. Add upgrade hooks and a healthcheck module to ensure safe rollouts and automatic rollback triggers.
design_decisions: Use provider aliasing for multi-account or multi-region tenants to avoid global provider reconfiguration.
Expose a stable set of inputs on the core module; avoid letting overlays mutate critical resource names or state keys.
Implement overlay precedence: core defaults < customer overlay (git) < local runtime patch (secrets-protected).
Version pin modules (semantic pinning) and allow compatible version ranges using a vendor manifest; vendoring available in private deployments for air-gapped upgrades.
Provide an upgrade hook interface in the module (pre_upgrade, post_upgrade) implemented as null_resource with local-exec that runs validation scripts, not imperative Terraform actions.
Healthchecks implemented as module-provided cloud-native probes & alerts plus a lightweight runtime readiness check registered in the console.
All Terraform applies require a signed plan artifact stored with the customer's installation metadata to aid audits and rollbacks.
State layout recommendation: single remote state per-customer deployment with explicit locking and an optional per-tenant sub-state for mutable runtime resources.
Automated terratest suite and a lightweight emulation harness (localstack or emulators) to validate overlays against the core module during CI.
Prefer computed outputs over direct resource references in overlays to reduce coupling and preserve upgrade safety.
acceptance_criteria: Core tenant module exposes stable inputs and documents which fields are safe to override.
Overlay merge tool (overlay-gen) exists and can take core tfvars, a git-hosted customer overlay, and a local patch to produce a final tfvars file and a reproducible plan artifact.
Upgrade flow: operator can run preflight, create a plan, and run a canary apply for 5% of traffic; healthchecks will trigger rollback on defined failure thresholds.
At least two customer-specific overlays validated in integration tests without requiring manual code changes to the core module.
Module version pinning and vendor manifest generation implemented and documented for private (air-gapped) installs.
Healthcheck module emits metrics/alarms that show up in Redwood Console and can be used to block rollout via guardrails.
Security checklist completed and security review approved for the overlay mechanism.
Runbook for emergency local patch apply and state migration documented and tested once in staging.
tasks: Prototype overlay-gen tool that merges tfvars and validates schema (owner: Diego).
Define core module stable input surface and mark internal outputs (owner: Asha).
Implement pre_upgrade/post_upgrade hook scaffolding and local-exec validators (owner: SRE team).
Create healthcheck module (owner: Observability team) with example CloudWatch/Stackdriver resources and console wiring.
Add vendor manifest support and a vendoring script for air-gapped installs (owner: Infra).
Write terratest cases for two representative customer overlays and add to CI (owner: Test infra).
Document runbook for state migration and emergency local patching (owner: Solutions Engineering).
